gen-dafont-starborn-gf-lisu-bosa: Starborn scatters its letters across wide stretches of blank space, with a dark, heavy band of lowercase running through each line. Starborn drifts and glows, while Lisu Bosa builds sturdy, generous words.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-montagu-slab: Starborn spreads its dreamy letters wide, laying a thick, dark stripe of lowercase through every line. Montagu Slab then steps in with robust downstrokes and a sizable x-height, giving the floaty heading something solid to land on.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-noto-serif-hentai: Starborn is all dreamy distance, with wide gaps between letters and a thick, dark stripe of lowercase in every line. Noto Serif Hentaigana counters with small letters rising almost to capital height and subtly shifting strokes.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-ovo: Starborn leaves huge gaps between its letters, and its thick, dark lowercase forms a stripe through every line. Ovo keeps thin strokes close to thick ones and ascenders shallow, so paragraphs would read with quiet authority.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-domine: Structural and striking, Stencilia leaves wide gaps at its curve terminals and squeezes its ascenders close to the x-height. Stencilia makes the statement, while Domine gives each curve room to breathe.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-headland-one: Striking, structural Stencilia leads with real presence. Headland One, a serif, settles underneath with a round o nearly matching its capital, generously spaced letters and mild thinning where curves turn.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-hedvig-letters-s: Stencilia leaves generous gaps where its curves end. Hedvig Letters Serif matches that openness with sturdy lowercase and moderate, readable contrast, so the two hold a page together without fighting.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-lisu-bosa: Stencilia keeps its curve terminals spacious and its ascenders tucked close to the x-height, giving every line a structural look. Lisu Bosa, meanwhile, makes words look large and sturdy, its counters spilling gently into the space around them.
gen-dafont-stencilia-gf-ovo: Thin strokes barely lighter than thick ones give the text a quiet authority, while Stencilia supplies the structure up top. Ovo carries heavier verticals, as if drawn with a gently tilted nib, against Stencilia's low-contrast strokes.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-esteban: Esteban keeps its thin parts only slightly slimmer than the stems, with a lowercase that looks oversized beside its capitals. Stentiga, meanwhile, stretches out in luxurious tracking, its crossbars matching its stems.
